question: When may you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed and gates are up.,b:If the lights have stopped flashing but the gate is still down.,c:If an approaching train seems far away.,d:Never — you must not go around a lowered gate.
note: Do not drive around or under a lowered gate; you must wait until lights and bells stop and the gate is fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only if you are on an expressway.,b:You may pass from your lane when traffic is clear.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: If the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross it to pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not pass another vehicle under which conditions?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:When a school bus's flashing red lights are on.,d:All of the above.
note: Never pass on hills or curves, at intersections, before or on railroad crossings or bridges, or when a stopped school bus has flashing red lights.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effects.,b:No — it has no effect on BAC.,c:Yes — it decreases BAC.
note: Coffee may make you feel more alert but it does not lower your blood alcohol concentration or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes (five seconds on a freeway), check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder.,b:Rely only on mirrors without checking your blind spot.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,d:Signal after you start the lane change.
note: Begin signaling in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to clear blind spots before completing a lane change.

question: How can alcoholic beverages affect your driving ability?
options: a:They slow reaction time, impair thinking and give false confidence.,b:They always make you more alert.,c:They improve coordination in small amounts.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows reflexes, impairs judgment and coordination, and can create a false sense of confidence.

question: How must a driver behave when encountering pedestrians?
options: a:Proceed unless the pedestrian is in your lane.,b:Assume pedestrians should yield to vehicles.,c:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid striking them.,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and take all reasonable actions to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is not lawfully crossing.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving typically:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or the vehicle.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs coordination, judgment, and reaction time; it reduces a driver's ability to operate a vehicle safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When, if ever, may you legally drive above the posted speed limit?
options: a:When no police officer is present to enforce the limit.,b:When surrounding traffic is driving above the limit.,c:Never; posted limits are the maximum under ideal conditions.
note: Speed limits represent the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions; you should not exceed them. You may need to go slower when conditions require it.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because visibility is reduced and headlights are required from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.,b:Because traffic moves much faster at night.,c:Because there is always more traffic at night.
note: At night you cannot see as well; use headlights appropriately and drive so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

question: If an approaching train is close enough or traveling fast enough to be hazardous, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: If a train is close enough to be a danger, do not attempt to cross the tracks. Wait until it has completely passed and all signals have cleared.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you finish the turn?
options: a:The lane closest to the lane you came from.,b:The rightmost lane.,c:Either lane indiscriminately.
note: Turn into the lane nearest to the one you left—on a left turn to a one-way street, that will be the leftmost available lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a driver's left arm and hand extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:They plan to turn right.,b:They plan to turn left.,c:They intend to come to a stop.,d:They plan to speed up.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver intends to slow or stop; adjust your driving accordingly if following such a vehicle.

question: On traffic signals mounted horizontally, where is the red light located?
options: a:The leftmost position.,b:The middle position.,c:The rightmost position.
note: Horizontal signals place the red light on the left, yellow in the middle, and green on the right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Only at red lights.,b:Only at stop signs.,c:At stop signs,d:Only if a police officer orders you to stop.
note: You must stop at intersections with stop signs or red lights and whenever a traffic officer instructs you to stop.

question: What happens to your field of vision as your vehicle speed increases?
options: a:It increases,b:It remains unchanged regardless of speed.,c:It decreases
note: As speed increases, your peripheral vision narrows and you must be more alert to potential hazards ahead and to the sides.

question: What color are signs that indicate public recreation or cultural sites?
options: a:Green.,b:Brown.,c:Orange.
note: Brown signs indicate areas of cultural or historical interest or public recreation, useful when traveling in unfamiliar areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left and opposing traffic blocks your view of other lanes, you should:
options: a:Accelerate quickly when the first lane clears.,b:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before turning.,c:Rely on another driver to wave you across.
note: Do not begin the left turn until you can see that all lanes you will cross are clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Stop on the shoulder to check traffic.,b:Always use cruise control while changing lanes.,c:Signal
note: On interstates, signal and verify mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes; only stop on the shoulder for emergencies.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Pass with caution whenever you want.,b:Slow down to below the speed limit.,c:Do not pass from your lane.
note: A solid yellow line adjacent to your lane indicates passing is prohibited from your direction.

question: On slippery roads, how should you handle turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly to avoid the curve.,c:Accelerate quickly through curves.
note: Reduce speed before and during turns on slippery roads to maintain traction and control.

question: Which practice helps prevent \highway hypnosis\" on long trips?"
options: a:Begin the trip well-rested and take regular stops.,b:Drive continuously without stopping to maintain focus.,c:Keep the cruise control engaged at all times.
note: To avoid highway hypnosis, start well-rested, take regular breaks even if you don't feel tired, and keep your eyes scanning the road.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren or flashing lights, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and slow down but not stop.,b:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.,c:Pull to the right and stop.,d:Speed up to clear the lane.
note: You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle using warning devices.

question: You must stop at a railroad crossing under which circumstances?
options: a:When flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only if you see a train approaching.,c:When directed to do so by a flagger or a stop sign.,d:Both a and b.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger or stop sign and when flashing red signals or gates are activated.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and yield, like a stop sign.,b:Proceed without stopping because the signal is broken.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping.
note: A flashing red signal mandates a full stop and yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you continue carefully through an intersection when the signal turns yellow?
options: a:If an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.,b:If you are already in the intersection when the light turns steady yellow.,c:If there are pedestrians crossing.
note: If you are already within the intersection when the light turns steady yellow, you should continue through carefully; do not enter on a yellow light if you can stop safely before the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn you must:
options: a:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Sound your horn to warn other drivers.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted in either direction.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway mean passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions except to turn.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.,b:Drive away if no one is nearby.,c:Leave a written notice with your name
note: If you cannot locate the owner after striking an unattended vehicle, leave a written notice with your contact information and the circumstances.

question: For drivers 21 and older, at what BAC is driving illegal in Louisiana?
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.05 percent.
note: Louisiana law makes it illegal for drivers 21+ to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to use a three-point turn (turnabout)?
options: a:Anytime you want to change direction quickly.,b:When driving in heavy,c:Only on a narrow street where a U-turn and going around the block are not possible.
note: Use a three-point turn only on a two-lane roadway when a U-turn is not possible and you cannot go around the block; it's the most difficult turnabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes into a solid green light, what applies to drivers who want to turn?
options: a:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,b:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:You retain automatic right-of-way to turn.
note: A green arrow gives protected turn movement. If it becomes a regular green, you may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question: Before making a turn, what action should you take?
options: a:Immediately turn the wheel without signalling.,b:Increase your speed then turn.,c:Signal at least three to four seconds before turning.
note: Activate your turn signal a few seconds before turning to notify other drivers and pedestrians of your intention.

question: What happens if you refuse a requested alcohol analysis test in Louisiana?
options: a:Refusal is recommended to avoid conviction.,b:You face no consequences.,c:Your license will be suspended (first offense results in 365-day suspension).
note: By law, driving in Louisiana implies consent to chemical testing. Refusing a test results in administrative license suspension (365 days for a first refusal).

question: If you find a defect that could affect safe vehicle operation, what should you do?
options: a:Drive only at reduced speeds until you can fix it.,b:Use the vehicle for short local trips only.,c:Delay repairs until you can afford them.,d:Have the defect repaired immediately before driving.
note: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be fixed as soon as possible and before driving when practical.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may park there if you remain in the vehicle.,b:You may stop only temporarily to load or unload passengers.,c:You may never stop your vehicle there.
note: A No Standing sign means you can stop briefly to pick up or discharge passengers, but you may not park.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:
options: a:All of the above.,b:Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.,c:Increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicles you are following.,d:Approach all vehicles with caution.
note: In snowy or icy weather keep windows and mirrors clear, increase following distance, and approach other vehicles and hazards with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign showing Reduced speed - 35 mph means:
options: a:You have ample time to slow before the reduced speed starts.,b:The reduced speed zone begins at the next sign.,c:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at that sign.
note: A Reduced speed sign indicates the new speed limit takes effect at the sign; reduce speed accordingly at that point.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what actions should you take?
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Turn off your radio and keep moving normally.,c:Speed up to cross before any approaching train arrives.,d:Look
note: Approach tracks with caution: look and listen for trains, slow down, and be ready to stop if necessary.

question: How should drivers depress the gas pedal?
options: a:With the heel lifted off the floor at all times.,b:By lightly tapping it.,c:Gradually and smoothly.,d:Abruptly to accelerate quickly.
note: Accelerate gradually and smoothly with the top of your foot on the gas pedal and your heel on the floor to maintain control.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?
options: a:Drive only on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your path.,c:Communicate your intentions to other road users (signal
note: Use signals, brake lights, and other communication methods to make your actions predictable and reduce the chance of misunderstandings that lead to crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you maintain?
options: a:A safe following distance from the vehicle ahead.,b:Decrease your following distance to fit into traffic.,c:Come to a complete stop before changing lanes.,d:Signal only after beginning the lane change.
note: Maintain a safe following distance, check mirrors and blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.
note: Most warning signs are yellow (often diamond-shaped) with black symbols or lettering, alerting drivers to unexpected road conditions.

question: As alcohol concentration in the blood increases, it generally:
options: a:Makes you more cautious and less confident.,b:Improves night vision.,c:Slows reactions
note: Higher blood alcohol slows reactions, lowers inhibition, and increases the likelihood of making dangerous driving decisions.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:You must stop and back up immediately.,b:Less-than-ideal driving conditions; slow down and use caution.,c:That it is summer.
note: Orange work zone signs warn of road work and changed traffic patterns; slow down, obey instructions, and be alert for workers and equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you need to change lanes, what is important to do?
options: a:All of the above,b:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.,d:Check your blind spot before moving.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with heavy oncoming traffic while the light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and block it until traffic clears.,b:Wait in the intersection or behind the crosswalk as appropriate until it is safe to turn.,c:Use the next intersection regardless of traffic signal rules.
note: You may enter the intersection to prepare for a left turn if the light is green, but you must wait until oncoming traffic clears before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should:
options: a:Pull off the roadway to let traffic pass when safe.,b:Continue at the same slow speed as you have the right to do.,c:Try to block the passing lane to prevent others from passing.
note: If you're impeding traffic on a two-lane road by driving much slower than the flow, pull off when safe to allow others to pass.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:Human error.,c:New drivers.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error — failing to see other vehicles, making poor decisions, or driving unsafely.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They always have the right-of-way.,b:They are harder to see and more vulnerable in traffic.,c:They always follow different traffic laws.
note: Smaller road users are more difficult to spot and are less protected; drivers should be vigilant to avoid collisions with them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to enter a freeway from an acceleration lane?
options: a:Drive slowly to better observe traffic and then merge.,b:Signal,c:Signal and enter; freeway traffic must yield.
note: When merging, match the speed of traffic as closely as possible, signal, and yield to oncoming vehicles already on the freeway.

question: A flashing red light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to others, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Proceed through at normal speed.,d:Turn right only.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

question: When confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, let them pass, and try to create distance.,b:Retaliate by tailgating to discourage them.,c:Cut them off to slow them down.
note: If another driver behaves aggressively, remain calm, do not engage, and put distance between you and the aggressor.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an approaching traffic light turns solid yellow as you near an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to get through before it turns red.,c:Ignore it and proceed as normal.
note: A solid yellow means the light is about to turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: If you are involved in a traffic accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Continue driving if no one looks hurt.,b:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.,c:Leave the scene and report it later.
note: If involved in an accident, you must stop at or near the scene, move your vehicle out of traffic if possible, and render aid within the limits of your ability.

question: Drivers may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant in Louisiana?
options: a:30 feet.,b:20 feet.,c:15 feet.
note: In Louisiana it is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant to allow access for emergency services.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.
note: Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel (into the skid) until traction returns, then correct steering to straighten the vehicle.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the 'P' stand for?
options: a:Prepare to pass.,b:Plan a route.,c:Pull over.,d:Predict hazards.
note: 'P' in SIPDE means 'Predict hazards' — anticipate the worst-case scenario and plan actions to stay safe.

question: Which description about work zones is correct?
options: a:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.,b:They are marked with black and white signs.,c:Work zones may be moving or stationary and require extra caution.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving (e.g., road crews); they are marked by orange signs and require drivers to slow down and pay close attention.

question: What do pentagonal signs (five-sided) typically indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones or school crossings.
note: Pentagonal signs are used to mark school zones and school crossing areas; watch carefully for children and crossing guards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are separated by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction.

question: When pedestrians are in marked crosswalks, which is true?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way.,b:No one has the right-of-way.,c:Pedestrians must always be given the right-of-way.,d:Only emergency vehicles must yield.
note: Marked crosswalks indicate where pedestrians should cross; drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs, posted on the left side of the roadway, warn of No Passing Zones and reinforce that passing is prohibited.

question: Which statement is true about even a small amount of alcohol?
options: a:Only a blood alcohol above the legal limit affects driving.,b:Alcohol has no effect on concentration.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can impair abilities needed to drive safely. No amount of alcohol is safe when driving.

question: What seasonal hazard is common in autumn?
options: a:Only an increase in daylight hours.,b:Decreased need for following distance.,c:Slick leaves on roadways.
note: Wet leaves can create slippery surfaces similar to ice; reduce speed and increase following distance when leaves are wet.

question: What is the maximum distance you may be parked from a curb when parallel parking (Louisiana)?
options: a:You must be within 10 inches of the curb.,b:You must be within 15 inches of the curb.,c:You must be within 18 inches of the curb.
note: When parallel parking, the vehicle's wheels should be no more than 18 inches from the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding can kill.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
note: Excessive speed increases the severity of crashes and fatalities. Both driving too fast and driving too slowly relative to traffic can be dangerous.

question: How do bridges and overpasses behave in winter weather?
options: a:They freeze after other roads.,b:They are unaffected by freezing temperatures.,c:They tend to freeze before and remain icy longer than other roadways.
note: Because they are exposed to cold air on both sides, bridges and overpasses can ice over sooner and stay icy longer than regular roadway surfaces.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.,b:Roll down your window and ask for directions.,c:Continue to the next exit and then safely return to your desired route.
note: Do not back up or attempt U-turns on the highway; go to the next exit and use it to return to the missed exit safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat an intersection protected by a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Stop as you would at a stop sign and proceed when safe.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
note: A flashing red light should be treated like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.

question: If your vehicle does NOT have ABS and you must stop quickly, you should:
options: a:Hold the brake pedal down continuously.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Firmly pump the brake pedal.
note: On vehicles without ABS, firmly pump the brakes to avoid locking the wheels while maintaining steering control in an emergency stop.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the approaching vehicle's wheels.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: When faced with oncoming high beams, glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded while still seeing enough to maintain your lane until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At intersections.,c:At railroad crossings.,d:All of the above.
note: It is unlawful and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which general rule should you remember about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow traffic as quickly as possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary.,c:Pass on the right whenever possible.
note: Passing increases crash risk. Drive with the traffic flow within speed limits and pass only when necessary and safe.

question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Following too closely.,b:Inattentive driving.,c:Excessive speed for conditions.
note: Major causes of crashes include speeding for conditions, inattention, and tailgating; any of these behaviors significantly raise crash risk.

question: Why must drivers be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They rarely use headlights.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,c:They are smaller and harder to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and more easily hidden in blind spots; their speed and distance can be harder to judge, so drivers should be extra cautious around them.

question: What factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:How much water they drank earlier.,b:Amount of food in the stomach,c:Only the drinker's tolerance.,d:Whether they are driving a manual or automatic vehicle.
note: BAC is affected by how much you drink, your weight, the time over which you drink, and whether you've eaten; food slows absorption but does not prevent impairment.

question: How would you describe distracted driving?
options: a:Not a serious concern.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers and others.,c:Very uncommon.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky and increases the likelihood of crashes involving drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and cyclists.

question: In bad weather, what should drivers do with their following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Maintain the same distance as in good conditions.
note: Reduce speed and increase following distance in adverse weather to give yourself more time to react and stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while driving on an interstate, what is the correct action?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Continue to the next exit and use it to reach your destination.,c:Make a U-turn to get back to the exit.
note: Do not stop, back up, or make illegal turns on the interstate. Continue to the next exit and re-route as needed.

question: What danger does a leaking exhaust system present?
options: a:Fumes can make you drowsy or cause death.,b:It causes excessive oil use.,c:It requires a tune-up sooner than normal.
note: Exhaust leaks can allow toxic fumes like carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment, which can cause drowsiness, illness, or death.

question: How should you check blind spots to avoid collisions?
options: a:Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.,b:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move.,c:Honk your horn right before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes or turning, physically turn your head and look over your shoulder to ensure the blind spot is clear; mirrors alone are not sufficient.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest relative speed to maintain?
options: a:Drive significantly slower than traffic to stay cautious.,b:Constantly vary speed to remain alert.,c:Drive faster than traffic to reduce time on the road.,d:Drive with the general flow of traffic within the posted limit.
note: Driving at a speed consistent with the flow of traffic (within the legal limit) reduces the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle that honks first has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle that is larger has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way.,d:The vehicle approaching from the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles approaching from your right if you arrive simultaneously.

question: When should vehicle occupants fasten safety belts?
options: a:Only when making sharp turns.,b:Only when traveling faster than 55 mph.,c:Before you start driving—Louisiana law requires all occupants to be properly buckled.
note: Louisiana law mandates that all occupants be secured with safety belts; ensure everyone is buckled before driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roundabout or rotary, drivers should:
options: a:Drive clockwise around the central island.,b:Yield to traffic entering the roundabout.,c:Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.
note: Drivers must yield to vehicles already in the roundabout and travel counterclockwise around the central island.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane on a roadway, which is the correct practice?
options: a:You may stop to look up an address.,b:You should not stop; keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.,c:You may make a U-turn or back up if you entered the wrong ramp.,d:You may stop briefly to drop off passengers.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road; if you miss an exit, go to the next one or a safe place to turn around.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may turn in the arrow's direction without caution.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,c:The arrow has no regulatory meaning.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that protection for the indicated turn is ending; slow and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.,b:Honk your horn at least three times.,c:Speed up and re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: When passing, check mirrors and blind spots, signal your lane change, and only re-enter when it is safe and you can see the passed vehicle ahead in your mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,b:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the signal allows you to proceed
note: A steady red signal requires you to stop. You may turn right on red where not prohibited, but only after a complete stop and if it is safe.

question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger’s directions and slow down when instructed.,b:Follow whatever surrounding traffic does regardless of the flagger.,c:Assume flaggers are optional and ignore them.
note: Obey flaggers and posted directions in work zones; they control traffic for safety of workers and drivers.

question: What is the proper method for looking while backing a vehicle?
options: a:Open your door to check behind you.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.
note: Before backing, check behind the vehicle and while reversing, turn to look through the rear window—do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

question: Diagonal stripes sloping downward to the left on a barricade indicate what?
options: a:Drivers should bear to the left.,b:Drivers must stop immediately.,c:Drivers should bear to the right.,d:The road ahead is closed.
note: Diagonal stripes indicate the direction drivers should move; stripes sloping down and left mean bear left.

question: What is the best practical way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive fast through puddles to clear water.,b:Keep cruise control on to maintain steady speed.,c:Use high beam headlights in rain.,d:Slow down when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.
note: To avoid hydroplaning, reduce speed in wet conditions and ensure tires have good tread and proper inflation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines the space you need to safely cross traffic?
options: a:Whether you signaled early enough.,b:Road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.,c:The presence of a stop sign only.
note: The gap you need depends on road surface, weather, and how much oncoming traffic there is.

question: If your wheels run off the paved roadway onto the shoulder, what should you do first?
options: a:Yank the steering wheel to force the tires back onto the road.,b:Brake hard and stop immediately.,c:Slow down gently and then steer back onto the pavement when safe.
note: If your vehicle leaves the pavement, remain calm, reduce speed by gently applying the brakes while keeping the wheels off the pavement. When you have slowed to a safe speed, steer back onto the roadway—do not jerk the wheel or make sudden moves.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the recommended course of action?
options: a:Lie down and sleep inside the car.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Stay in your car,d:Stand in the road to attract attention.
note: If stranded in a snowstorm, remain in your vehicle, conserve heat, and wait for rescue; you are more likely to be found if you stay with the car.

question: Railroad crossings should always be considered:
options: a:Dangerous and requiring caution.,b:Appropriate places to park temporarily.,c:Safe to cross because trains are rare.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous. Look, listen, and obey all signals before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may a driver pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?
options: a:When the car in front is waiting to turn left.,b:When the shoulder is paved and clear.,c:When the car in front is driving under the speed limit.,d:Never; passing on the shoulder is prohibited.
note: Passing by driving on the shoulder is not allowed; other drivers do not expect vehicles on the shoulder and it is unsafe.

question: Alcohol in the bloodstream primarily:
options: a:Has no effect on driving at low doses.,b:Slows reflexes and reaction time.,c:Wakes you up and improves focus.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain functions needed for safe driving, reducing reaction time and judgment.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:Beer lessens impairment compared to wine.,b:Wine reduces impairment compared to beer.,c:Impairment depends on the amount of alcohol consumed, not the type of beverage.
note: Impairment is related to the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream, regardless of whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor.

question: In fog, what should you do regarding speed and headlights?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit if visibility seems fine.,b:Turn on hazard lights and turn off low beams.,c:Use high beams to see further in fog.,d:Drive cautiously at reduced speed and use low beam headlights.
note: In fog, reduce speed, drive cautiously, and use low beams, since high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up your vehicle, what is the recommended practice?
options: a:Look over your shoulder through the rear window.,b:Rely solely on a backup camera.,c:Rely only on your mirrors.
note: Turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window when backing up. Do not rely solely on mirrors or cameras.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:One driver may continue without stopping.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right; then proceed when safe.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness when driving faster on a wet roadway?
options: a:Tire traction decreases and risk of hydroplaning increases.,b:Water has no effect if your tires are good.,c:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires lose ability to clear water and may hydroplane, reducing control.

question: If you must drive in fog, what should you do first?
options: a:Use high beam headlights for better visibility.,b:Turn on hazard lights only.,c:Drive at the maximum speed limit.,d:Turn on low beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog and reduce speed; don't use high beams because they cause glare and reduce visibility.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Pedestrian crosswalks only.,b:Railroad crossings where you must yield to trains.,c:School zones.,d:No passing zones.
note: Crossbuck signs indicate a railroad crossing and require drivers to yield to trains and proceed only when safe.

question: Which best describes driving as an activity?
options: a:An automatically easy task anyone can do without practice.,b:A complex skill that is mastered over time and requires attention.,c:Always very simple regardless of conditions.
note: Driving is a complex skill that requires ongoing practice, attention, and respect for safety rules.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams and fog lights in fog; high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility further.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving best described?
options: a:A serious traffic safety problem that impairs safe driving.,b:A minor traffic safety issue if only a few drinks are consumed.,c:Safe as long as you feel okay to drive.
note: Driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs is dangerous and significantly reduces driving ability, endangering you and others.

question: Which in-vehicle distraction increases crash risk the most?
options: a:Eating a sandwich quietly.,b:Playing the CD player.,c:Using a cell phone.,d:Listening to the radio.
note: Cell phone use (including hands-free) is a major distraction and significantly increases crash risk.

question: What does an orange traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A railroad crossing ahead.,b:A construction or maintenance area.,c:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange signs indicate construction, maintenance, or emergency operations. Use extra caution and obey posted instructions.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks and you cannot free it, you should:
options: a:Turn off the ignition carefully, apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe area.,b:Slam on the brakes while steering abruptly.,c:Open the hood immediately while driving to inspect the throttle.
note: If the accelerator sticks, shift to neutral, turn off the ignition without locking the steering, apply brakes, and steer safely off the road.

question: When a curb is painted yellow, what does that indicate?
options: a:Short parking stops only.,b:Accessible parking.,c:A loading zone or another parking restriction.
note: A yellow-painted curb usually denotes loading zones or other parking restrictions where stopping or parking is limited.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic signal mean for left turns?
options: a:You should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction immediately.,b:You must come to a complete stop.,c:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns but requires you to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before completing the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:
options: a:The posted minimum speed limit.,b:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for current conditions.,c:The posted maximum speed limit regardless of conditions.
note: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for the conditions (weather, traffic, road quality) even if that is below the posted limit.

question: What should drivers remember about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger cars.,c:They need no extra space to turn compared to passenger cars.
note: Trucks have large blind spots on several sides and require more distance to stop and more space to maneuver than smaller vehicles; avoid lingering near them.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs tell drivers?
options: a:They are placed only where a present danger exists.,b:They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.,c:They indicate what a driver must or must not do.
note: Regulatory signs instruct drivers about laws and regulations, such as speed limits, no-turn zones, and yield or stop requirements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're stopped in a line at a stop sign and the cars ahead have cleared the intersection with no cross traffic, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping again.,b:Bring your vehicle to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping the second time.,d:Honk and proceed.
note: You must always come to a full stop at a stop sign and yield to any cross traffic before proceeding, even if the vehicle ahead has already gone through.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check blind spots before maneuvers called?
options: a:A dangerous maneuver.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:Unnecessary scanning.,d:Checking your blind spot — a good driving habit.
note: Turning your head to check blind spots is a good, necessary habit when changing lanes, merging, or pulling away from a curb.

question: Which actions improve safety when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and ensure headlights are functioning properly.,b:Drive if you are very tired but keep windows open.,c:Use only parking lights.,d:Turn on interior lights to read maps.
note: At night, increase following distance, avoid driving tired, and make sure headlights are properly aimed and working.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol, certain medications (legal or illegal), and lack of sleep.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only physical injuries.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and fatigue; be aware of your condition before driving.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed if you do not see a train.,b:Stop and look for a train, remaining at least 15 feet from the nearest rail.,c:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.
note: If warning signals are flashing at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and do not proceed until it is safe.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for what characteristic of large vehicles?
options: a:Smaller blind spots than passenger cars.,b:Increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:Decreased stopping distance compared to cars.,d:Less noise and vibration.
note: Large vehicles require greater stopping distances; other drivers should allow extra space and avoid lingering in truck blind spots.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your rearview mirror.,b:Your seat belt.,c:Your seat position.
note: Begin by adjusting your seat so you can reach controls and see clearly; after seating position is set, adjust mirrors and steering column if needed.

question: At dusk or on overcast days you should:
options: a:Drive using only parking lights.,b:Turn on your headlights (low beams) to increase visibility.,c:Use four-way flashers while moving.
note: Turn on headlights at dusk or when visibility is reduced; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet of following traffic.

question: If you are involved in a collision, which of the following actions should you take?
options: a:Call the police or request emergency services if needed.,b:All of the above,c:Stop immediately.,d:Help the injured if you can.
note: If involved in an accident stop, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, assist the injured within your ability, and call police or emergency services when necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your turn signals are not working, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use proper hand signals.,b:Use your horn.,c:Use your headlights.,d:Flash your brake lights repeatedly.
note: If turn signals fail, use standard hand signals to indicate turning intentions to other road users.

question: Doubling a car's speed increases the force of impact by about how much?
options: a:Two times.,b:Depends only on vehicle weight.,c:Three times.,d:Four times.
note: Kinetic energy (and potential force of impact) increases with the square of speed; doubling speed increases impact force about fourfold.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane (the nearest appropriate lane).,b:The middle lane by default.,c:Any lane as long as you signal.,d:The far right lane only.
note: When turning onto a multi-lane street, enter the lane nearest to the one you came from and avoid lane changes immediately after turning.

question: What do diagonal stripes sloping down to the right on a barricade or panel tell drivers?
options: a:They indicate you must stop.,b:They indicate you should bear to the right.,c:They indicate you should bear to the left.
note: Diagonal stripes on barricades or vertical panels guide traffic direction; stripes sloping down to the right tell drivers to pass to the right (stripes sloping down left direct drivers left).

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Never; they must yield to you.,b:Whenever you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,c:Only when they are directly behind you.,d:Only if other vehicles have already yielded.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or sirens by pulling over and stopping.

question: Which statement about drowsy driving is true?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio will reliably prevent drowsiness.,b:Drowsy drivers can appear to be intoxicated due to poor driving.,c:Drinking strong coffee is an effective long-term solution.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving to the point that the driver appears drunk. Short measures like radio or coffee are inadequate; rest is required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time and that vehicle is to your right, you should:
options: a:Speed up to beat them through the intersection.,b:Proceed and force the other vehicle to stop.,c:Honk and proceed.,d:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When is it appropriate to honk your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you have lost control of your vehicle and to warn of immediate danger.,b:To signal your annoyance at a slow driver.,c:While passing another car on a two-lane road.,d:To express thanks after they yield.
note: Sound your horn only to warn others of danger or when necessary to avoid a crash, such as if you lose control.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing your lane from the lane you want to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Broken white line.,b:Double solid yellow line.,c:Solid yellow line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when it is safe.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and remain in your lane.,b:Pull to the right curb and stop promptly.,c:Keep driving and let it pass on either side.,d:Accelerate to clear the intersection.
note: When an emergency vehicle is using its lights or siren, immediately pull to the right and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When roads are slippery, what should you do with your following distance?
options: a:Increase the following distance to allow more time to stop.,b:Keep the same following distance as on dry roads.,c:Decrease your following distance to keep traffic flowing.
note: On slippery roads increase the gap between you and the vehicle ahead because stopping distances are longer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you?
options: a:No passing is allowed.,b:The road is a one-way road.,c:The road is a two-way road with traffic moving in both directions.,d:The road is temporarily closed.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed when safe.

question: What does fluorescent yellow-green sign color indicate?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:Pedestrian,c:Hospitals.
note: Fluorescent yellow-green is used for pedestrian, bicycle, and school-area warning signs to alert drivers to higher pedestrian activity or special hazards.

question: If a vehicle is tailgating you and there's no right lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to increase the gap.,b:When safe,c:Brake abruptly to discourage tailgating.,d:Ignore them and maintain speed.
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot move right, slow down gradually when safe to let the tailgater pass; never brake suddenly.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive more quickly to clear the hazardous area sooner.,b:Drive the posted speed limit exactly.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce your speed at the first sign of rain, snow, or sleet to maintain traction and control.

question: When driving under non-ideal conditions, what minimum following distance should you keep?
options: a:Three seconds.,b:One second.,c:Two seconds.
note: When conditions are not ideal (weather, road, traffic), increase your following distance to at least four seconds; three seconds is minimal for normal conditions.

question: What must you do when you encounter a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when the way is clear.,b:Slow down and drive through the intersection.,c:Stop only if other vehicles are present.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should do what?
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road and merge safely when possible.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Proceed without stopping if they think it's clear.,d:Have the right-of-way over traffic on the public road.
note: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, yield to vehicles already on the public road and merge only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking near a crosswalk, how close may you legally park to the crosswalk?
options: a:No closer than 10 feet.,b:No closer than 5 feet.,c:No closer than 20 feet.
note: In Louisiana it is illegal to park within 20 feet of a crosswalk; keep that minimum distance to ensure visibility and pedestrian safety.

question: To ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe, you should:
options: a:Only drive when your physical condition is perfect.,b:Ignore side effects of medicines if you feel fine.,c:Know how any medicine affects your driving
note: Be aware of medical conditions and drug effects; only drive if you can do so safely within your physical limitations.

question: What should happen to your following distance when driving in snowy weather?
options: a:Keep it the same as in dry conditions.,b:Decrease it because vehicles stop faster in snow.,c:Increase it—allow more space between you and the vehicle ahead.
note: On snow or ice you need much more space to stop; increase following distance accordingly.

question: When are seat belts most effective?
options: a:All occupants in the vehicle should wear seat belts.,b:Passengers should wear seat belts only on long trips.,c:Only the driver should wear a seat belt.
note: Every person in the vehicle should wear a seat belt. Unrestrained occupants can become projectiles during a crash and can injure others.

question: How must drivers respond to a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
options: a:Pass cautiously at slow speed.,b:Proceed if you think most children are done exiting.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn.,d:Honk before passing the bus on the left.
note: When a school bus displays its stop signal, drivers must stop and wait until the arm is withdrawn and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the right lane of the one-way street.,c:In the center of the one-way street.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the leftmost lane (the lane closest to the one you left).

question: The Highway Transportation System consists of which main components?
options: a:People only.,b:Vehicles only.,c:People, vehicles, and roads.
note: The HTS is made up of people, vehicles, and roads — all interacting together to move people and goods.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply away from the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: When parked facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which actions should you perform when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Signal,b:Check only your side view mirror.,c:Check only your rearview mirror.,d:Quickly turn your head without signaling.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to ensure your blind spot is clear.

question: On a horizontal traffic signal, which position is the green light in?
options: a:On the right.,b:In the middle.,c:On the left.
note: On horizontal signals the lights are arranged left to right: red, yellow, green, with the green typically on the right.

question: What color combination do most warning signs use to indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white.,b:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,c:White letters on a blue background.
note: Warning signs that indicate hazards ahead are typically yellow with black symbols or lettering; work zones use orange with black.

question: When are headlights legally required in Louisiana?
options: a:When the driver is tired.,b:When the temperature drops below freezing.,c:Between sunset and sunrise.
note: Louisiana law requires headlights between sunset and sunrise; also use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or following within 200 feet.

question: You hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway. What should you do?
options: a:Disregard the signal if other lanes are available.,b:Stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow, move to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop when safe.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or sirens, slow, move to provide a clear path, and stop if necessary to allow it to pass.

question: How should a seat belt be positioned?
options: a:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.,b:Loose and comfortable.,c:Hidden beneath the seat cushion.
note: Lap belts should lie across the hips and lower abdomen; shoulder belts should fit across the chest and shoulder for proper protection.

question: What is road rage considered under the law?
options: a:Merely an annoyance.,b:A criminal offense that can lead to serious legal consequences.,c:An acceptable response to poor driving by others.
note: Road rage can escalate into criminal behavior; individuals involved may face legal penalties if incidents become violent or dangerous.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Sitting with the engine running in drive.,b:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.,c:Accelerating quickly.
note: Looking ahead to avoid sudden stops and accelerating smoothly conserves fuel; hard accelerations and idling waste gasoline.

question: What does an \End school zone\" sign communicate?"
options: a:That the speed limit is 20 mph.,b:The end of a reduced-speed school zone.,c:The beginning of a reduced-speed school zone.
note: An \End school zone\" sign indicates the reduced school-zone speed limit is ending and the regular speed limit resumes."

question: You are about to back out of a driveway and see children playing nearby. Before moving your car you should:
options: a:Sound your horn to warn them.,b:Assume the children will hear you and back up slowly.,c:Walk to the back of the car and check that the way is clear.
note: Before backing, get out and visually check behind the vehicle for children and obstacles rather than relying only on mirrors or sounds.

question: How are smoking and preparing to smoke while driving classified?
options: a:Actions that help maintain alertness.,b:Activities that do not affect driving.,c:Distracting activities that can reduce safety.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by taking your hands or eyes off the road and increases crash risk.

question: When may you legally cross solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction at any time.,b:Only when making a left turn or entering/exiting a driveway where permitted.,c:During daylight hours only.
note: As a general rule, solid center lines should not be crossed except when making a permitted left turn or entering/exiting a driveway.

question: Why should you exercise extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are deaf and cannot hear your horn.,b:They are a police officer.,c:They are signaling to stop traffic.,d:They are likely blind and may need the right-of-way and extra time to cross.
note: Pedestrians with white canes or guide dogs are blind; slow, yield, and be prepared to stop to avoid injuring them.

question: Which behavior is commonly associated with road rage?
options: a:Keeping a safe distance from other cars.,b:Flashing headlights to warn others.,c:Deliberately obstructing other vehicles.
note: Road rage behaviors include deliberately obstructing vehicles, tailgating, cutting off other drivers, and aggressive gestures. Give space and avoid retaliation.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what documents must the driver produce?
options: a:Only proof of insurance.,b:Only proof of registration.,c:Driver license
note: When stopped, the driver must be prepared to present a valid license, current registration, and proof of insurance; keep these documents in the vehicle when driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should a driver do?
options: a:Yield to all other drivers always.,b:Maintain speed and proceed.,c:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to stop.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to vehicles from the right and be prepared to slow or stop to avoid collisions.

question: When a curb is painted white, what does it indicate?
options: a:Accessible parking only.,b:It marks a loading zone or other restriction.,c:Only short parking stops are permitted.
note: White curb paint indicates areas where only short stops are allowed; other colors (like yellow) indicate different restrictions.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Safely pull to the curb, stop, and look to see if the vehicle is approaching on your street.,b:Keep driving until you see the vehicle, then pull over.,c:Slow down but continue driving until you find it.
note: If you hear emergency sounds and cannot tell where they are, pull to the right and stop until you can confirm the vehicle's location and it has passed.

question: How should you pass an animal on the roadway if safe to do so?
options: a:Sound your horn repeatedly to scare it away.,b:Pass slowly and cautiously so you don't startle it.,c:Pass as closely as possible at normal speed.
note: When animals are on the road, slow down and pass carefully to avoid frightening them into unpredictable movement.

question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Apply the parking brake.,b:Firmly apply your brakes immediately.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On slick surfaces first remove your foot from the accelerator; if further slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.,b:Either one may proceed first.,c:The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left.,d:The larger vehicle always yields.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Which light at an intersection indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A solid yellow light.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: What habits are important to maintain when driving on major highways?
options: a:Glance at one point on the road for long periods to avoid distraction.,b:Stay alert,c:Constantly drive at the same speed without scanning.
note: On highways avoid 'highway hypnosis' by keeping your eyes moving, staying alert, and being prepared to respond to unexpected hazards.

question: If a police officer stops you, what is the recommended behavior?
options: a:Get your paperwork out and show it before the officer approaches.,b:Remain in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,c:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower the window.
note: Remain in the vehicle with your hands visible. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance before retrieving them.

question: What color are highway destination and exit signs that show distances?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Red with white letters.,c:Yellow with black letters.,d:Black with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are green with white letters or symbols.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive and may lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Beer,b:Illegal drugs and certain prescription medications.,c:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,d:All of the above
note: Alcohol, illegal drugs, certain prescription and over-the-counter medicines, and inhalants can all impair driving and may lead to DUII.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Only when pulling toward a curb.,b:Whenever you are changing lanes or moving your vehicle's position.,c:Only when turning left or right at intersections.
note: Check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder each time you change lanes, turn, or pull to/away from curbs to ensure no vehicles are there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light requires you to:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,c:Proceed slowly and with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means caution; slow down, look carefully for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Open the window and drive on.,b:Stop driving and rest.,c:Get some coffee and continue driving.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similarly to alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving, rest, or change drivers.

question: What should drivers do before starting a turn?
options: a:Immediately accelerate into the turn.,b:Always come to a complete stop before turning.,c:Slow down before making the turn.
note: Slowing down significantly before a turn is the safest and smoothest method; entering a turn too fast can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can completely pass through.,b:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you to show you are waiting.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for it to clear.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through it; blocking the intersection is illegal and unsafe.

question: What is the meaning of fluorescent pink traffic signs?
options: a:Incident management signs.,b:School zone signs.,c:Speed limit signs.
note: Fluorescent pink is used for temporary incident management signs that warn drivers of nonpermanent issues such as crash scenes or emergency-related closures.

question: What minimum following distance should you maintain when following a motorcycle?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Three seconds.,c:Four seconds.
note: Increase your following distance to at least four seconds behind a motorcycle to allow extra time and space if the rider falls or must stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line when:
options: a:Turning left into a driveway.,b:Passing a disabled vehicle in front of you.,c:Doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: A broken line may be crossed to pass or change lanes only if it can be done safely and without interfering with other traffic.

question: When driving where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:That a child could run into the road without checking for traffic.,b:Children will always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Children will know when it is safe to cross.
note: Children are unpredictable and may run into the street without looking—slow down and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Only use the outside rearview mirror.,b:Use only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turn your head to look over your shoulder and check the blind spot.
note: Turn your head to check blind spots before every lane change; mirrors do not show all areas beside and behind your vehicle.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.,b:Slow down but remain in your lane.,c:Motion for the vehicle to pass you on your left.
note: Yield immediately to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; if in an intersection, clear it then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the primary purpose of an advisory speed or speed restriction sign for curves and turns?
options: a:To be ignored in rainy,b:To indicate the sign is blue with black lettering.,c:To show a recommended safe speed for that curve or turn.
note: Advisory speed signs indicate recommended speeds for curves and turns; you should reduce your speed further in adverse conditions.

question: What is meant by a truck's \No zone\"?"
options: a:A safety buffer that cars should drive in.,b:The blind spot around a large vehicle.,c:A designated no-passing zone.
note: \No zones\" are the large blind spots around trucks and other large vehicles; avoid lingering there where the driver cannot see you."

question: Which curb color indicates a fire zone where parking is restricted?
options: a:Blue.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.,d:White.
note: Painted curbs indicate parking restrictions; a red curb indicates a fire lane or fire zone where parking is prohibited.

question: Regulatory road signs are generally what color and must always be obeyed?
options: a:Green.,b:White.,c:Blue.
note: Regulatory signs, such as speed limits and stop signs, are usually white (with black markings) and must be obeyed.

question: Which of the following is true about passing safely?
options: a:You need not signal if traffic is clear.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes and check mirrors and blind spots.,c:Return to your lane immediately after passing without checking.
note: Before passing, signal in advance, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots; return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: A solid white centerline on a two-lane road indicates:
options: a:Lanes move opposite and passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or prohibited.,c:Lanes move in opposite directions and you may pass at will.
note: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction; a solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling nearby, what should you do to assist it?
options: a:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,b:Speed up to get out of its way.,c:Stop and prevent it from passing.
note: If safe to do so, pull to the side and provide a clear path for emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

question: If taking a non-prescription drug, what should a driver do before driving?
options: a:Ignore labels and drive as usual.,b:Drink alcohol to counter side effects.,c:Read the labels for warnings about driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medications can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure about driving while on the medicine.

question: What pavement markings or signals are sometimes used to direct drivers into proper turning lanes on highways?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road only.,b:No markings are used for this purpose.,c:Arrow markings on the pavement and lane-control arrows.,d:Flashing red lights above every lane.
note: Arrows on pavement or lane-control arrows indicate which lanes are designated for turning or through traffic.

question: What is the purpose of highway markings?
options: a:They are usually unimportant.,b:They provide information and guidance for drivers.,c:They are only for construction zones.
note: Markings show lane boundaries, passing zones, and warnings, helping drivers position their vehicles and navigate safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection controlled by a stop sign but with no marked stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and ensuring it is safe.,b:After slowing but not stopping if no other vehicles are present.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet from the intersection whether necessary or not.
note: If there's no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and go only when it is safe to do so.

question: What do two solid yellow lines in the center of the roadway indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is allowed only when at the top of a hill.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: Two solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that no vehicle in either direction may cross the lines to pass (except to turn into a driveway or private road where permitted).

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A deaf person.,b:A person in a traffic study.,c:A blind person.
note: A white cane or guide dog usually identifies a person as blind; drivers must yield to and be cautious around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return immediately after passing.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Remain in the left lane if you plan to turn left soon.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, ensuring a safe distance to re-enter the lane.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:Only the color of the vehicle.,c:The driver’s height.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, the condition of brakes and tires, and road surface conditions, among other factors.

question: Where is it particularly important to slow down?
options: a:Only on highways.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:On narrow or winding roads
note: Reduce speed on narrow/winding roads, near intersections/rail crossings, on hills/curves, where pedestrians or hazards exist, and in poor weather.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Do not immediately apply the brakes; gradually slow and pull off the road.,b:Increase speed to reach a service area sooner.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the gas, hold the steering wheel firmly, avoid braking suddenly until under control, then slow and pull off safely.

question: In the SIPDE process, what does the \D\" represent?"
options: a:Defensive driving.,b:Dodge.,c:Decide on a safe action.
note: SIPDE stands for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute; the \D\" is to decide on the safest action to take."

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:Only the bicycle lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width just like any other vehicle and should not be driven in a portion of a lane.

question: What does an arrow painted in a lane indicate?
options: a:Drivers in that lane must make the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers may optionally make the movement indicated by the arrow.,c:Drivers must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: A pavement arrow indicates the required movement for drivers in that lane; follow any traffic signals or signs before completing the turn or maneuver.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,b:Always stop whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.,d:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.
note: Be alert for children and be ready to stop; yield to pedestrians in or about to enter crosswalks.

question: When adjusting the inside rearview mirror, what should you be able to see?
options: a:Only the road directly behind the car.,b:The entire rear window without moving your head.,c:The passengers in the backseat only.,d:Your own reflection clearly.
note: Adjust the inside mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat by moving only your eyes, not your head.

question: What is true about driving while distracted?
options: a:It usually causes drivers to drive faster and more safely.,b:It usually causes drivers to react more slowly to hazards.,c:It is never dangerous.,d:It improves multitasking skills.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction times and increases the likelihood of a crash; it is never safe.

question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow and a red light allows you to:
options: a:Go straight only and wait for a solid green to turn.,b:Ignore the arrow and follow the red light.,c:Proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow
